title: A and the semicolon
summary: The little fingers, the last two home-row keys, and the first real English words.
intro: Little fingers are the weakest of the eight, and they are asked to do a surprising amount of work: A, the semicolon, and later Shift, Enter and most of the punctuation. Start them off properly now and the rest of the course is much easier. With A in place you have every vowel the home row offers, which means that from the middle of this lesson you stop typing patterns and start typing words.
congrats: Eight keys, eight fingers, and you have typed English. The word list was short because the home row alone is short — the next three lessons add six more keys and it opens up quickly.

screens.text: Left little finger, at the far left of the middle row. It is a small, weak finger doing a full-sized job; give it its own movement rather than swinging the whole hand.
The whole left hand, one finger per key, outward and back. This is the shape your left hand will hold for the rest of the course.
screens.content:
sdaf fsda
dfs klj df
af fa afaf

screens.text: Right little finger. The semicolon is where your right hand rests, the mirror of A — and in a moment it becomes the anchor for reaching the punctuation further out.
The right hand now has its full shape too. Both little fingers on the outside, both index fingers on their bumps.
All eight keys of the home row, which is what "home row" means: the row your hands live on.
screens.content:
adsf afsd
ldk jas ld
df fd dfdf
fff ssss dddd aaa

screens.text: Mixed, both hands. Let the fingers pick the keys; you pick the pace.
Real English words, all of them typed without your hands leaving the home row. There are not many yet — that is honestly all eight keys can make.
screens.content:
dad as salads asks
fad lass falls adds
lads fall alas ask

screens.text: The same words as a burst. Whole words now, not letters — read the word, then type it, rather than reading one letter at a time.
Notice what changed: you are thinking about words, and your fingers are handling the letters. That is the whole goal of the course, arriving early.
screens.content:
ad alas salad
add ask flasks
fads sad lass

screens.text: Back to the little fingers on their own for a moment. They are the ones that will slow you down later if they are neglected now.
screens.content:
a;a;a; ;a;a;a
s;al l;as
asd lf; as

screens.text: Last one. Next lesson reviews all eight keys before the course starts reaching off the row.
